0.label: tapper_head_with_collars
0.description: The upper part of the tapper's grip: incised ring collars below the smooth point, then a face with a cross-hatched coiffure.
0.iconography: The head on an ìróké marks the tapper's 'person' — the devotee or Ọ̀rúnmìlà's messenger — facing out while the point strikes the tray.

1.label: tapper_crosshatched_base
1.description: The base of the tapper: a cylinder covered in diagonal cross-hatching, like netting or basketry.
1.iconography: Woven pattern on the grip — the same net diaper that fills tray rims and post shafts.

panel.title: Modakeke Ifá tapper: point, face, kneeling figure, netted base
panel.summary: A single tapper photographed on its own: a smooth tapering point, ring collars, a face in a cross-hatched cap, a kneeling figure, and a netted base. It is the leftmost of the four on FoA_04-5598, or a close twin.

register_readings.reading: Collars and a face at the top of the grip.
The netted base; the kneeling figure between (undetected).

panel.composition: Vertical stacking of point, collars, head, kneeling body and textured base — the standard tapper grammar.
panel.narrative: An instrument of address: the point strikes the tray to call Ifá, while the carved devotee kneels in respect. It belongs with the Modakeke diviner's kit.
uncertainties: May duplicate one tapper on FoA_04-5598.
